newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Tuesday on short-covering after continued losses over the past few trading days, traders said.
The key July 1997 contract ended at 3,396 yuan ($409) per tonne, rising six yuan. It opened at 3,400 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,420 and a low of 3,360.
May fell 57 yuan to 3,303, September rose five to 3,420, and November put on 35 to 3,430.
Combined volume rose to 17,100 tonnes from 14,100.
Traders said short-covering dominated Tuesday's trading, but most investors remaining sidelined.
"Today's gains were a rebound from the losses of the past few days," one traders said. "But most investors are still sidelined on a lack of market-moving news."
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate around the 3,400 yuan level in the next few days.
